subject: chem
title: Chemical Bonding & Molecular Structure
syllabus: Kossel - Lewis approach to chemical bond formation, the concept of ionic and covalent bonds. Ionic Bonding: Formation of ionic bonds, factors affecting the formation of ionic bonds; calculation of lattice enthalpy. Covalent Bonding: Concept of electronegativity. Fajan's rule, dipole moment: Valence Shell Electron Pair Repulsion (VSEPR) theory and shapes of simple molecules. Quantum mechanical approach to covalent bonding: Valence bond theory - its important features, the concept of hybridization involving s, p, and d orbitals; Resonance. Molecular Orbital Theory - Its important features, LCAOs, types of molecular orbitals (bonding, antibonding), sigma and pi-bonds, molecular orbital electronic configurations of homonuclear diatomic molecules, the concept of bond order, bond length, and bond energy. Elementary idea of metallic bonding. Hydrogen bonding and its applications.

topics.lewis: Lewis structures, formal charge & bond parameters

body: Ionic bond: electron transfer (large electronegativity difference); covalent: electron sharing. Lattice enthalpy measures ionic strength.
Octet rule exceptions: incomplete (BF_{3}, BeCl_{2}), odd-electron (NO, NO_{2}, ClO_{2}), expanded (PCl_{5}, SF_{6}, H_{2}SO_{4}).
Formal charge = valence e^{−} − non-bonding e^{−} − number of bonds
Fajans: small, highly charged cation + large anion → more covalent character (AlCl_{3}, LiI). Bond order up → bond length down, bond energy up.
lone pairs = ½(valence e^{−} of centre − charge − e^{−} used in bonds) (F, Cl, H use 1; =O uses 2)

Steric number = σ bonds + lone pairs → 2 linear (sp), 3 trigonal (sp^{2}), 4 tetrahedral (sp^{3}), 5 trigonal bipyramidal (sp^{3}d), 6 octahedral (sp^{3}d^{2}), 7 pentagonal bipyramidal (sp^{3}d^{3}).
Repulsion: lp–lp > lp–bp > bp–bp. In a trigonal bipyramid lone pairs go EQUATORIAL: 4+1 see-saw (SF_{4}), 3+2 T-shape (ClF_{3}), 2+3 linear (XeF_{2}).
In an octahedron: 5+1 square pyramidal (BrF_{5}, XeOF_{4}), 4+2 square planar (XeF_{4}, ICl_{4}^{−}).
More lone pairs squeeze the angle: CH_{4} 109.5° > NH_{3} 107° > H_{2}O 104.5°.
More electronegative outer atoms pull bond pairs away → smaller angle: NF_{3} (102°) < NH_{3}; OF_{2} (103°) < H_{2}O < Cl_{2}O (111°, bulky Cl).
Going down a group (same shape) the angle falls: NH_{3} > PH_{3} > AsH_{3} (≈ 90°, nearly pure p).
μ = q × d (debye; 1 D = 3.336 × 10^{−30} C m). Vector sum of bond dipoles (and lone-pair dipoles).
μ = 0 for symmetric shapes with identical ligands: CO_{2}, BF_{3}, CH_{4}, PCl_{5}, SF_{6}, XeF_{2}, XeF_{4}.
NH_{3} (1.47 D) ≫ NF_{3} (0.24 D): in NH_{3} lone-pair and bond dipoles add; in NF_{3} they oppose.
H-bond: H on N, O, F. Intermolecular raises bp (H_{2}O, HF, NH_{3}); intramolecular (o-nitrophenol) lowers bp and solubility.
AOs combine when energies are close and they have the SAME symmetry about the bond axis (e.g. 2s with 2p_{z}).
Order up to 14 e^{−} (B_{2}, C_{2}, N_{2}): σ1s σ*1s σ2s σ*2s (π2p_{x} = π2p_{y}) σ2p_{z} (π*) σ*. From O_{2} on, σ2p_{z} drops below π2p.
Bond order = ½(N_{b} − N_{a})

traps: Lone pairs in a trigonal bipyramid sit EQUATORIAL (ClF₃ is T-shaped, not trigonal planar).
XeF₂ and XeF₄ have lone pairs yet μ = 0 — symmetry wins.
NF₃ has a much smaller dipole than NH₃.
O₂⁺ and O₂⁻ have the same number of unpaired electrons (1).
[Co(NH₃)₆]³⁺ is d²sp³ (inner d), SF₆ is sp³d² (outer d).
o-Nitrophenol: intramolecular H-bond → more volatile than p-nitrophenol.

steps.note: Formal charge, shapes, hybridisation, bond angles

pyq.q: The number of molecules/ion/s having trigonal bipyramidal shape is: PF_{5}, BrF_{5}, PCl_{5}, [PtCl_{4}]^{2−}, BF_{3}, Fe(CO)_{5}
sol: PF_{5}, PCl_{5} (sp^{3}d, no lone pair) and Fe(CO)_{5} (dsp^{3}) are trigonal bipyramidal → 3.
BrF_{5} is square pyramidal, [PtCl_{4}]^{2−} square planar, BF_{3} trigonal planar.

pyq.q: Among SO_{2}, NF_{3}, NH_{3}, XeF_{2}, ClF_{3} and SF_{4}, the hybridization of the molecule with nonzero dipole moment and highest number of lone-pairs of electrons on the central atom is
sol: Lone pairs on the centre: SO_{2} 1, NF_{3} 1, NH_{3} 1, XeF_{2} 3 (but linear → dipole 0), ClF_{3} 2, SF_{4} 1.
Polar with most lone pairs: ClF_{3} (T-shaped, sp^{3}d).

pyq.q: Which among the following molecules is (a) involved in sp^{3}d hybridization, (b) has different bond lengths and (c) has lone pair of electrons on the central atom ?
sol: SF_{4}: 4 bonds + 1 lone pair → sp^{3}d, see-saw: two axial S−F bonds are longer than the two equatorial ones.
XeF_{2} is sp^{3}d but both bonds are axial (same length); PF_{5} has no lone pair; XeF_{4} is sp^{3}d^{2}.

pyq.q: Match the LIST-I with LIST-II. List-I (Molecules/ion): A. PF_{5}, B. SF_{6}, C. Ni(CO)_{4}, D. [PtCl_{4}]^{2−}. List-II (Hybridisation of central atom): I. dsp^{2}, II. sp^{3}d, III. sp^{3}d^{2}, IV. sp^{3}. Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
sol: Ni(CO)_{4}: Ni(0), CO pairs the 4s electrons into 3d → sp^{3} tetrahedral; [PtCl_{4}]^{2−}: Pt(II) d^{8} → dsp^{2} square planar.

pyq.q: Given below are two statements : Statement (I) : For ClF_{3}, all three possible structures (lone pairs both equatorial — I; one axial, one equatorial — II; both axial — III) may be drawn. Statement (II) : Structure III is most stable, as the orbitals having the lone pairs are axial, where the lp-bp repulsion is minimum. In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below :
sol: Three arrangements can be drawn (I true).
Lone pairs prefer EQUATORIAL positions (fewer 90° repulsions) → structure I (T-shape) is most stable; II is wrong.
o: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct

pyq.q: Number of molecules/ions from the following in which the central atom is involved in sp^{3} hybridization is: NO_{3}^{−}, BCl_{3}, ClO_{2}^{−}, ClO_{3}^{−}

Match List-I with List-II. List-I: (A) ICl, (B) ICl_{3}, (C) ClF_{5}, (D) IF_{7}. List-II: (I) T-shape, (II) Square pyramidal, (III) Pentagonal bipyramidal, (IV) Linear. Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
sol: ICl: a diatomic → linear. ICl_{3}: 3 bp + 2 lp → T-shape. ClF_{5}: 5 bp + 1 lp → square pyramidal. IF_{7}: 7 bp → pentagonal bipyramidal.

pyq.q: Given below are two statements: Statement I: PF_{5} and BrF_{5} both exhibit sp^{3}d hybridisation. Statement II: Both SF_{6} and [Co(NH_{3})_{6}]^{3+} exhibit sp^{3}d^{2} hybridisation. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :
sol: BrF_{5}: 5 bp + 1 lp = 6 → sp^{3}d^{2} → I false.
[Co(NH_{3})_{6}]^{3+} is a low-spin inner-orbital complex: d^{2}sp^{3}, not sp^{3}d^{2} → II false.
o: Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true

pyq.q: Match the LIST-I with LIST-II. LIST-I (Molecule/ion): A. ICl_{2}^{−}, B. H_{2}O, C. SO_{2}, D. XeF_{4}. LIST-II (Bond pair : lone pair on the central atom, counting each double bond as two bond pairs): I. 4 : 2, II. 4 : 1, III. 2 : 3, IV. 2 : 2. Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
In SO_{2}, NO_{2}^{−} and N_{3}^{−} the hybridizations at the central atom are respectively :
sol: N_{3}^{−} (N=N^{+}=N^{−}): central N has 2 σ, no lone pair → sp (linear).

pyq.q: The correct increasing order for bond angles among BF_{3}, PF_{3} and ClF_{3} is :
sol: BF_{3} trigonal planar 120°; PF_{3} pyramidal ≈ 98°; ClF_{3} T-shaped, F−Cl−F ≈ 87.5° (squeezed by two lone pairs).

pyq.q: In which one of the following pairs the central atoms exhibit sp^{2} hybridization?
sol: NH_{2}^{−} and H_{2}O are sp^{3} (2 σ + 2 lp).

pyq.q: SF_{4} is isostructural with: A. BrF_{4}^{−} B. CH_{4} C. IF_{4}^{+} D. XeF_{4} E. XeO_{2}F_{2}. Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
sol: SF_{4}: 4 bp + 1 lp → see-saw.
IF_{4}^{+} (4 + 1) and XeO_{2}F_{2} (4 + 1) are see-saw too. BrF_{4}^{−}, XeF_{4}: square planar; CH_{4}: tetrahedral.

pyq.q: Identify from the following species in which d^{2}sp^{3} hybridization is shown by central atom:
sol: d^{2}sp^{3} uses INNER (n − 1)d orbitals — only possible in low-spin complexes such as [Co(NH_{3})_{6}]^{3+} (Co^{3+}, d^{6}, strong-field NH_{3}).
BrF_{5} and SF_{6} use outer d (sp^{3}d^{2}); [PtCl_{4}]^{2−} is dsp^{2}.

pyq.q: The molecules having square pyramidal geometry are
sol: BrF_{5}: 5 bp + 1 lp; XeOF_{4}: 5 σ + 1 lp → both square pyramidal.
SbF_{5}, PCl_{5}: trigonal bipyramidal.

pyq.q: Consider 'n' is the number of lone pair of electrons present in the equatorial position of the most stable structure of ClF_{3}. The ions from the following with 'n' number of unpaired electrons are A. V^{3+} B. Ti^{3+} C. Cu^{2+} D. Ni^{2+} E. Ti^{2+}. Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
sol: ClF_{3}: both lone pairs equatorial → n = 2.

pyq.q: Number of compounds with one lone pair of electrons on central atom amongst following is: O_{3}, H_{2}O, SF_{4}, ClF_{3}, NH_{3}, BrF_{5}, XeF_{4}
sol: One lone pair: O_{3}, SF_{4}, NH_{3}, BrF_{5} → 4.

pyq.q: According to Lewis theory, the total number of σ bond-pairs and lone pair of electrons around the central atom of XeO_{6}^{4−} ion is ____.
sol: XeO_{6}^{4−}: Xe (8) + 4 extra = 12 electrons, all used in 6 bonds → 6 σ pairs, 0 lone pairs → 6.

pyq.q: Match List-I with List-II. List-I (Molecule): (A) BrF_{5}, (B) H_{2}O, (C) ClF_{3}, (D) SF_{4}. List-II (Shape): (I) T-shape, (II) See saw, (III) Bent, (IV) Square pyramidal.
sol: BrF_{5} square pyramidal, H_{2}O bent, ClF_{3} T-shaped, SF_{4} see-saw.

pyq.q: The molecule/ion with square pyramidal shape is:
sol: BrF_{5}: 5 bp + 1 lp → square pyramidal.

pyq.q: Consider the following species: BrF_{5}, XeF_{5}^{−}, BF_{4}^{−}, ICl_{4}^{−}, XeF_{4}, SF_{4}, NH_{4}^{+}, ClF_{3}, XeF_{2}, ICl_{2}^{−}. Number of species having sp^{3}d hybridized central atom is ____ .

Among the following, the CORRECT combinations are A. IF_{3} → T-shaped (sp^{3}d) B. IF_{5} → Square pyramidal (sp^{3}d^{2}) C. IF_{7} → Pentagonal bipyramidal (sp^{3}d^{3}) D. ClO_{4}^{−} → Square planar (sp^{2}d). Choose the correct from the options given below :
sol: IF_{3}: 3 + 2 → T-shaped, sp^{3}d ✓. IF_{5}: 5 + 1 → square pyramidal, sp^{3}d^{2} ✓. IF_{7}: 7 + 0 → pentagonal bipyramidal, sp^{3}d^{3} ✓.
ClO_{4}^{−}: 4 σ, no lone pair → tetrahedral (sp^{3}) ✗.

pyq.q: Bromine trifluoride autoionizes to form BrF_{2}^{⊕} and BrF_{4}^{⊖}. The shapes of the cation and anion are respectively ____, and ____.
sol: BrF_{2}^{+}: 7 − 1 − 2 = 4 electrons → 2 lone pairs + 2 bonds → bent.
BrF_{4}^{−}: 7 + 1 − 4 = 4 → 2 lone pairs + 4 bonds → square planar.

pyq.q: Given below are two statements : Statement I : The number of compounds among SO_{2}, SO_{3}, SF_{4}, SF_{6} and H_{2}S in which sulphur does not obey the Octet rule is 3. Statement II : Among [H_{2}O, ClF_{3}, SF_{4}], [NH_{3}, BrF_{5}, SF_{4}], [BrF_{5}, ClF_{3}, XeF_{4}] and [XeF_{4}, ClF_{3}, H_{2}O], the number of sets in which all the molecules have one lone pair of electrons on the central atom is 1. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :
sol: In their usual Lewis structures S has more than 8 electrons in SO_{2} (10), SO_{3} (12), SF_{4} (10) and SF_{6} (12) → 4, not 3 → I false.
Only [NH_{3}, BrF_{5}, SF_{4}] has one lone pair on every central atom → II true.
o: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true

pyq.q: Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R). Assertion (A): PH_{3} has lower boiling point than NH_{3}. Reason (R): In liquid state NH_{3} molecules are associated through vander waal's forces, but PH_{3} molecules are associated through hydrogen bonding. In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
sol: NH_{3} boils higher because IT is hydrogen-bonded; PH_{3} has only van der Waals forces. A true, R reversed (false).
o: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct

pyq.q: Select the compound from the following that will show intramolecular hydrogen bonding.
sol: o-Nitrophenol: the −OH and −NO_{2} sit next to each other, so the H bonds to an O of NO_{2} INSIDE the same molecule (a 6-membered ring).
H_{2}O, NH_{3}, ethanol show intermolecular H-bonds.

pyq.q: Given below are two statements. Statement I: The dipole moment of CH_{3}−CH=CH−CH=O is greater than CH_{3}−CH_{2}−CH_{2}−CH=O. Statement II: C_{1}−C_{2} bond length of CH_{3}−CH=CH−CH=O is greater than C_{1}−C_{2} bond length of CH_{3}−CH_{2}−CH_{2}−CH=O. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
sol: Conjugation pulls electron density along the chain to O (CH_{3}−CH^{+}−CH=CH−O^{−} form) → bigger dipole: I true.
The same resonance gives C_{1}−C_{2} partial double-bond character → SHORTER: II false.
o: Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
Both Statement I and Statement II are true

pyq.q: The correct statement/s about Hydrogen bonding is/are : A. Hydrogen bonding exists when H is covalently bonded to the highly electro negative atom. B. Intermolecular H bonding is present in o-nitro phenol C. Intramolecular H bonding is present in HF. D. The magnitude of H bonding depends on the physical state of the compound. E. H-bonding has powerful effect on the structure and properties of compounds. Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
sol: A ✓ (H on F, O, N). B ✗ (o-nitrophenol: intramolecular). C ✗ (HF: intermolecular). D ✓ (strongest in solid, weakest in gas). E ✓.

pyq.q: Number of compounds/species from the following with non-zero dipole moment is: BeCl_{2}, BCl_{3}, NF_{3}, XeF_{4}, CCl_{4}, H_{2}O, H_{2}S, HBr, CO_{2}, H_{2}, HCl
sol: Symmetric (μ = 0): BeCl_{2}, BCl_{3}, XeF_{4}, CCl_{4}, CO_{2}, H_{2}.
Polar: NF_{3}, H_{2}O, H_{2}S, HBr, HCl → 5.

pyq.q: Which one of the following molecules has maximum dipole moment?
sol: CH_{4}, PF_{5}: symmetric (0). NF_{3}: bond dipoles oppose the lone-pair dipole (0.24 D). NH_{3}: they add up (1.47 D) → maximum.

pyq.q: Given below are two statements : one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R). Assertion (A) : NH_{3} and NF_{3} molecule have pyramidal shape with a lone pair of electrons on nitrogen atom. The resultant dipole moment of NH_{3} is greater than that of NF_{3}. Reason (R) : In NH_{3}, the orbital dipole due to lone pair is in the same direction as the resultant dipole moment of the N − H bonds. F is the most electronegative element. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :
sol: In NH_{3} the lone-pair and N−H dipoles point the same way (add); in NF_{3} the N−F dipoles point away from the lone pair (cancel partly). R explains A.
o: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)

pyq.q: Number of compounds from the following with zero dipole moment is ____. HF, H_{2}, H_{2}S, CO_{2}, NH_{3}, BF_{3}, CH_{4}, CHCl_{3}, SiF_{4}, H_{2}O, BeF_{2}
sol: CHCl_{3} is tetrahedral but with mixed atoms → polar.

pyq.q: Given below are two statements : one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R). Assertion (A): Cis form of alkene is found to be more polar than the trans form. Reason (R): Dipole moment of trans isomer of 2-butene is zero. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :
sol: In trans-2-butene the two C−CH_{3} bond dipoles point opposite ways and cancel (μ = 0); in cis they add. So cis is more polar, explained by R.
o: Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)

pyq.q: Number of molecules from the following which can exhibit hydrogen bonding is ____. CH_{3}OH, H_{2}O, C_{2}H_{6}, C_{6}H_{6}, o-nitrophenol, HF, NH_{3}
sol: Need H on N, O or F: CH_{3}OH, H_{2}O, o-nitrophenol (intramolecular), HF, NH_{3} → 5.

pyq.q: Arrange the following compounds in increasing order of their dipole moment : HBr, H_{2}S, NF_{3} and CHCl_{3}

Which of the following statement is true with respect to H_{2}O, NH_{3} and CH_{4} ? A. The central atoms of all the molecules are sp^{3} hybridized. B. The H−O−H, H−N−H and H−C−H angles in the above molecules are 104.5°, 107.5° and 109.5°, respectively. C. The increasing order of dipole moment is CH_{4} < NH_{3} < H_{2}O. D. Both H_{2}O and NH_{3} are Lewis acids and CH_{4} is a Lewis base. E. A solution of NH_{3} in H_{2}O is basic. In this solution NH_{3} and H_{2}O act as Lowry-Bronsted acid and base respectively. Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
sol: A ✓ (all steric number 4). B ✓ (more lone pairs → smaller angle). C ✓ (0 < 1.47 < 1.85 D).
D ✗ (H_{2}O, NH_{3} are Lewis BASES). E ✗ (NH_{3} is the base, H_{2}O the acid).
o: A, B, C and E Only

pyq.q: Among H_{2}S, H_{2}O, NF_{3}, NH_{3} and CHCl_{3}, identify the molecule (X) with lowest dipole moment value. The number of lone pairs of electrons present on the central atom of the molecule (X) is :
sol: Lowest μ: NF_{3} (0.24 D). Its central N has 1 lone pair.

pyq.q: Given below are statements about some molecules/ions. Identify the CORRECT statements. A. The dipole moment value of NF_{3} is higher than that of NH_{3}. B. The dipole moment value of BeH_{2} is zero. C. The bond order of O_{2}^{2−} and F_{2} is same. D. The formal charge on the central oxygen atom of ozone is −1. E. In NO_{2}, all the three atoms satisfy the octet rule, hence it is very stable. Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
sol: D ✗ (central O of O_{3} is +1). E ✗ (NO_{2} has 17 electrons — an odd-electron molecule).

pyq.q: Given below are two statements : Statement I: F_{2}O < H_{2}O < Cl_{2}O is the correct trend in terms of bond angle. Statement II : SiF_{4}, SnF_{4} and PbF_{4} are ionic in nature. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :
sol: Bond angles: OF_{2} ≈ 103°, H_{2}O 104.5°, Cl_{2}O ≈ 111° (big Cl atoms push apart) → I true.
SiF_{4} is a covalent gas (only SnF_{4}, PbF_{4} are ionic) → II false.
o: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true

pyq.q: Which of the following molecule(s) show/s paramagnetic behavior? A. O_{2} B. N_{2} C. F_{2} D. S_{2} E. Cl_{2}. Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
sol: O_{2} and S_{2} (same valence count) have two unpaired π* electrons → paramagnetic.
N_{2}, F_{2}, Cl_{2}: all paired.

pyq.q: Number of molecules having bond order 2 from the following molecule is ____. C_{2}, O_{2}, Be_{2}, Li_{2}, Ne_{2}, N_{2}, He_{2}
sol: Bond orders: C_{2} 2, O_{2} 2, Be_{2} 0, Li_{2} 1, Ne_{2} 0, N_{2} 3, He_{2} 0 → 2 molecules.

pyq.q: Total number of electron present in (π^{*}) molecular orbitals of O_{2}, O_{2}^{+} and O_{2}^{−} is

Given below are two statements : Statement (I) : The correct sequence of bond lengths in the following species is : O_{2}^{+} < O_{2} < O_{2}^{−} < O_{2}^{2−}. Statement (II) : The correct sequence of number of unpaired electrons in the following species is : O_{2} > O_{2}^{+} > O_{2}^{−} > O_{2}^{2−}. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :
sol: Bond orders 2.5, 2, 1.5, 1 → lengths increase in that order: I true.
Unpaired: O_{2} 2, O_{2}^{+} 1, O_{2}^{−} 1, O_{2}^{2−} 0 — O_{2}^{+} and O_{2}^{−} are EQUAL, so the strict order fails: II false.
o: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true

pyq.q: Which of the following linear combination of atomic orbitals will lead to formation of molecular orbitals in homonuclear diatomic molecules [internuclear axis in z-direction]? A. 2p_{z} and 2p_{x} B. 2s and 2p_{x} C. 3d_{xy} and 3d_{x^{2}−y^{2}} D. 2s and 2p_{z} E. 2p_{z} and 3d_{x^{2}−y^{2}}. Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
sol: Orbitals combine only if they have the same symmetry about the bond (z) axis.
2s and 2p_{z} are both symmetric about z (σ) ✓. 2p_{x} with 2p_{z} or 2s: overlap cancels. d_{xy} and d_{x^{2}−y^{2}}: different symmetry (zero net overlap).

pyq.q: Given below are two statements : Statement (I): Experimentally determined oxygen-oxygen bond lengths in the O_{3} are found to be same and the bond length is greater than that of a O=O (double bond) but less than that of a single (O−O) bond. Statement (II): The strong lone pair-lone pair repulsion between oxygen atoms is solely responsible for the fact that the bond length in ozone is smaller than that of a double bond (O=O) but more than that of a single bond (O−O). In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :
sol: Ozone's two O−O bonds are equal (128 pm) and in between single (148) and double (121) — I true.
The cause is RESONANCE (bond order 1.5), not lone-pair repulsion; II also mis-states the comparison → false.
o: Statement I is false but Statement II is true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Both Statement I and Statement II are true

pyq.q: Sum of bond order of CO and NO^{+} is
sol: CO and NO^{+} are isoelectronic with N_{2} (14 electrons): bond order 3 each → 6.

pyq.q: Total number of molecules/species from following which will be paramagnetic is: O_{2}, O_{2}^{+}, O_{2}^{−}, NO, NO_{2}, CO, K_{2}[NiCl_{4}], [Co(NH_{3})_{6}]Cl_{3}, K_{2}[Ni(CN)_{4}]
sol: O_{2}, O_{2}^{+}, O_{2}^{−}, NO (11 valence e^{−}), NO_{2} (odd electron) are paramagnetic; CO is not.
[NiCl_{4}]^{2−}: tetrahedral Ni^{2+} d^{8}, 2 unpaired ✓; [Co(NH_{3})_{6}]^{3+} low-spin d^{6} and [Ni(CN)_{4}]^{2−} square planar d^{8} are diamagnetic → 6.

pyq.q: The number of species from the following which are paramagnetic and with bond order equal to one is: H_{2}, He_{2}^{+}, O_{2}^{+}, N_{2}^{2−}, O_{2}^{2−}, F_{2}, Ne_{2}^{+}, B_{2}
sol: Bond order 1: H_{2}, O_{2}^{2−}, F_{2}, B_{2}. Of these only B_{2} (π_{x}^{1}π_{y}^{1}) is paramagnetic → 1.

pyq.q: The total number of anti bonding molecular orbitals, formed from 2s and 2p atomic orbitals in a diatomic molecule is
sol: 2s + 2s → σ, σ*. Three 2p pairs → σ, σ*, two π, two π*.
Antibonding: σ*2s, σ*2p, π*2p_{x}, π*2p_{y} → 4.

pyq.q: The total number of molecules with zero dipole moment among CH_{4}, BF_{3}, H_{2}O, HF, NH_{3}, CO_{2} and SO_{2} is
sol: μ = 0: CH_{4}, BF_{3}, CO_{2} → 3. SO_{2} is bent (polar).

pyq.q: The total number of molecular orbitals formed from 2s and 2p atomic orbitals of a diatomic molecule is ____.
sol: Each atom brings 4 orbitals (2s + three 2p) → 8 atomic orbitals → 8 molecular orbitals.

pyq.q: The linear combination of atomic orbitals to form molecular orbitals takes place only when the combining atomic orbitals A. have the same energy B. have the minimum overlap C. have same symmetry about the molecular axis D. have different symmetry about the molecular axis. Choose the most appropriate from the options given below:
sol: Conditions: comparable energy, same symmetry about the axis, MAXIMUM overlap → A and C.

pyq.q: Pair of species among the following having same bond order as well as paramagnetic character will be-
sol: O_{2}^{+}: 2.5, 1 unpaired. N_{2}^{−}: 2.5, 1 unpaired → same.

pyq.q: Given below are two statements: Statement I: The number of species among BF_{4}^{−}, SiF_{4}, XeF_{4} and SF_{4} that have unequal E−F bond lengths is two. Here, E is the central atom. Statement II: Among O_{2}^{−}, O_{2}^{2−}, F_{2} and O_{2}^{+}, O_{2}^{−} has the highest bond order. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below
sol: Only SF_{4} (see-saw) has two kinds of S−F bonds; the others are symmetric → one, not two: I false.
o: Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true

pyq.q: The formal charges on the atoms marked as (1) to (4) in the Lewis representation of HNO_{3} molecule H−O(1)−N(2)(=O(3))−O(4) respectively are
sol: Formal charge = valence e^{−} − nonbonding e^{−} − bonds.

pyq.q: Identify the molecule (X) with maximum number of lone pairs of electrons (obtained using Lewis dot structure) among HNO_{3}, H_{2}SO_{4}, NF_{3} and O_{3}. Choose the correct bond angle made by the central atom of the molecule (X).
sol: F−N−F angle ≈ 102°.

pyq.q: The covalent radii of atoms A and B are r_{A} and r_{B}, respectively. The covalent bond length and total length of AB molecule are respectively
sol: Bond length = distance between nuclei = r_{A} + r_{B}.
End to end: r_{A} (beyond A) + (r_{A} + r_{B}) + r_{B} (beyond B) = 2(r_{A} + r_{B}).
